_comment: Thirty-six questions somebody might ask the stylist. Twenty have one right
answer that can be counted off the wardrobe fixture; sixteen do not.
The sixteen negatives are the important half. `facts.ts` says the router is
closed and that an unmatched question goes to the model unchanged — so the
measurement that matters is not how many lookups it catches, it is how many
TASTE questions it wrongly answers with arithmetic. A wedding-outfit question
answered with an inventory count is worse than the same question costing an
AI call, because the user cannot tell it went wrong.
Two cases are annotated knowing the router disagrees with them today, and
both are left in:
sf-019  'which top do I wear least' — 'wear least' is not in the intent
table (only 'least worn' / 'wear the least' shapes are), so a real
lookup escapes to the model. A recall miss: it costs a call.
sf-033  'what would you wear with a leather jacket in autumn' — 'wear with'
matches the compatible rule, so a request for an opinion comes back
as a count of pieces at the same formality. The expensive error.
`grounded` holds substrings that must appear in the answer, and every one of
them is arithmetic over the fixture rather than a phrasing preference: the
wardrobe has three white tops, two pairs of shoes, one dress. If a future
answer reworded itself entirely but kept the numbers, this corpus still
passes — which is right, because the number is the thing a model would have
got wrong.
